title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A Multiwavelength Study of its 2026 Giant X-ray Outburst
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 17 pages, 11 figures
summary: GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. We analyse three NuSTAR observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented by archival RXTE and Chandra data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. NuSTAR observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of $(-5.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-8}$ s s$^{-1}$ during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3-79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe K$α$ emission line, with no evidence for a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirms the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through H$α$ and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart is detected, with a $3σ$ upper limit of 36 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$ at 1.28 GHz. Weaker H$α$ emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit.

title: Magnetar X-ray flares as elementary reconnection events in a self-organized critical magnetosphere
summary: Magnetar bursts are commonly attributed to magnetic energy release, yet the physically relevant dissipation unit has remained uncertain. Here we argue that this unit is not the burst as conventionally defined, but the short substructures within bursts, namely magnetar X-ray flares (MXFs). Using 789 MXFs from SGR~J1935+2154, we show that their waiting times separate into two components, interpreted as reflecting clustered intra-episode events and longer inter-episode intervals, that their proxy emission measure and temperature exhibit distinct rising and declining trends, and that their energy release scale (ERS) proxy distribution has a high-end slope in the same statistical regime as solar and stellar flares. Combined with the previously measured MXF duration slope, these results identify MXFs as a three-dimensional fractal-diffusive self-organized critical (FD-SOC) system with $β_{\rm diff}\simeq2$, implying reconnection avalanches that expand linearly through an active magnetosphere. We infer that magnetar active episodes are global unloading states assembled from many elementary flares. Magnetar X-ray flares are therefore the physically relevant units for magnetar outburst statistics and for connecting magnetar high-energy activity to other impulsive phenomena.

title: Revisiting the Multiwavelength Data of GRB 240825A: Implications for a Two-Stage Central Engine and a Dusty Environment
comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Reanalyzing the multi-wavelength data of GRB 240825A, we identify two distinct prompt-emission episodes, i.e. an early, spectrally soft plateau and a subsequent bright, spectrally hard gamma-ray pulse. We show that this signature is consistent with a two-stage central engine model, in which the early soft plateau is powered by the dipolar spin-down radiation of a transient proto-magnetar, while the later hard pulse arises from a relativistic jet launched by fallback accretion onto the nascent black hole via the Blandford-Znajek mechanism. Adopting simulation-motivated initial black hole (BH) masses ($M_{\rm BH,0}$) and spins ($a_0$), our fits to the second episode yield total masses supplied to the post-collapse disk of $M_{\rm fb}=0.45$--$0.96 M_\odot$, fallback radii of $r_{\rm fb}=16.9$--$17.6 r_g$, and characteristic fallback timescales of $t_{\rm fb}=0.13$--$0.25$ s. The corresponding maximum inner accretion rates range from $0.18$ to $0.70 M_\odot \mathrm{s}^{-1}$, which is sensitive to $a_0$. Joint spectral fits with optical-X-ray afterglow data reveal a coupled temporal evolution of dust extinction and equivalent hydrogen column density. Incorporating this extinction evolution, an external forward-reverse shock model in a wind-like medium can account for the radio-to-GeV band afterglow data. Although ambient dust and the bright host galaxy may obscure any associated supernova, late-time optical reddening remains compatible with a supernova contribution. Applying the empirical relation between the prompt spectral peak energy and the SN peak bolometric magnitude gives an illustrative estimate of $M_{\rm bol,peak}=-19.46\pm0.35$ mag for a putative associated SN. These results support a two-stage evolution of the central engine and variable dusty environment of GRB 240825A, which provides insights into the nature of its progenitor.

title: Bayesian exploration of weakly interacting models of dark matter admixed neutron stars based on multi-density constraints
summary: We present a unified Bayesian analysis of Higgs-portal, neutron-decay, and axion-like-particle (ALP)-mediated dark matter in neutron stars within the single-fluid approximation. Using a common relativistic mean-field description of hadronic matter, we combine finite-nucleus and heavy-ion collision data, chiral effective field theory, NICER measurements of four pulsars, and GW170817. The individual dark-sector parameters remain weakly determined, while model-dependent shifts in nuclear skewness reveal the sensitivity of the inferred hadronic equation of state to the assumed dark-matter mechanism. The three scenarios yield substantially overlapping mass-radius and tidal-deformability predictions, with median maximum masses near $2.1\,M_\odot$. For $1.4\,M_\odot$ stars, the Higgs-portal model predicts higher $f$-mode frequencies and shorter damping times than the neutron-decay and ALP models, although their credible regions overlap. Comparison with three consistently reanalysed two-fluid models gives the largest Bayesian evidence to neutron decay: under the adopted priors, its Bayes factors relative to the Higgs-portal and two-fluid alternatives are approximately $24$-$37$, but only $2.2$ relative to ALP. This ranking concerns complete dark-matter models and does not establish a general preference for either fluid description or evidence for a dark component itself. Improved nuclear constraints and future gravitational-wave asteroseismology could provide complementary information to disentangle the hadronic and dark-sector contributions.

title: Rotating Vector Model predictions in millisecond pulsar magnetospheres with dipole and quadrupole field components
comment: To be submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. Comments welcome
summary: The rotating vector model (RVM) is widely used to interpret pulsar radio polarization under the assumption of a dipolar magnetic field. Motivated by tentative evidence for non-dipolar magnetic structure in millisecond pulsars provided by recent modeling of surface thermal X-ray pulsations, we examine how a global quadrupole component modifies position-angle (PA) behavior within the classical RVM framework. We numerically integrate magnetic field lines in static vacuum magnetospheres composed of a centered dipole component that is inclined with respect to the spin axis, and a centered quadrupole component aligned with it. We then compute the open field line regions (OFLRs), emission skymaps, and PA curves for a range of dipole inclinations, relative quadrupole strengths, and light cylinder radii corresponding to two trial spin periods of 1\,ms and 5\,ms. We find that quadrupole-modified magnetospheres produce a wide variety of PA behaviors and substantially alter the morphology and total area of OFLRs, with the OFLR area varying non-monotonically with quadrupole strength and, in some cases, exceeding that of the corresponding pure dipole. Depending sensitively on the field configuration and viewing geometry, three broad PA regimes can be distinguished: a) nearly dipolar PA swings that are largely insensitive to emission altitude; b) moderately distorted, altitude-dependent PA tracks that can bias dipolar RVM fits; and c) strongly dispersed PA behavior associated with emission from different OFLRs, which can remain incompatible with a single dipolar PA track even within narrow emission altitude ranges. These results demonstrate that dipole-like PA curves do not uniquely imply a purely dipolar magnetic field, while global quadrupole components alone are insufficient to reproduce the full complexity of observed millisecond pulsar PA profiles.

title: The Thousand-Pulsar-Array programme on MeerKAT - XX. Co-existing interacting periodicities and polarization modulation in PSR J1901-0906
comment: 19 pages, 16 figures and 3 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of the complex subpulse modulation in PSR J1901-0906 using data from the Thousand-Pulsar-Array (TPA) programme. Our analysis reveals the coexistence of three distinct periodicities in the subpulse modulation of both profile components, which obey a beat relation. We also detect additional spectral beat features caused by the modulation of these co-existing periodicities by investigating the Fourier phase correlation in two-dimensional fluctuation spectra. Moreover, the single-pulse polarization states are shown to be modulated and synchronized with the three co-existing periodicities observed in total intensity. Such synchronization has been reported for only a small number of pulsars, but this discovery marks the only one where this synchronization involves multiple co-existing periodicities. The modulation beats are similar to, yet more complex than, the beat system previously identified in PSR J1514-4834 with higher-order harmonics playing a significant role. The coexistence of the observed beat-like periodicities in PSR J1901-0906 implies that they are not independent, but rather originate from an underlying, interconnected physical system within the pulsar magnetosphere. Building upon the same geometric framework previously applied to PSR J1514-4834, we demonstrate that a feedback system with interacting rotating carousels successfully reproduces the complex subpulse modulations observed in PSR J1901-0906 and naturally explains the beat relations.

title: Radio and Gamma-Ray Timing of a Newly Discovered Millisecond Pulsar
summary: We report the discovery and timing of PSR J2147-3604, a fully recycled millisecond pulsar with a spin period of 3.2 ms, discovered in a reprocessing of the 350-MHz Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey and later serendipitously confirmed by the MeerKAT TRAPUM UHF survey of Fermi-LAT unidentified sources. We followed up this pulsar with Murriyang/Parkes radio telescope and obtained a phase-connected timing solution spanning one year, revealing a 4.5-day binary orbit with very low eccentricity (e ~ 1.9 x $10^{-5}$). A follow-up search in LAT data revealed gamma-ray pulsations, allowing for a joint radio and gamma-ray timing analysis. Assuming a neutron-star mass of 1.5 Msun, the inferred median companion mass (~0.2 Msun) is consistent with a helium white dwarf. The pulsar has a low dispersion measure of 17.0 pc cm$^{-3}$ and shows strong scintillation, leading to it being detected in ~72% of the observations covering the 704-1174 MHz band with Murriyang. The pulsar has a narrow duty cycle of ~6.5%, which leads to individual time of arrival (ToA) uncertainties of ~4.5 us for a 10 min integration with MeerKAT, suggesting this pulsar is well suited for inclusion in PTA experiments.

title: Discovery of 51 pulsars in a reanalysis of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap Survey and a revised pulsar census
summary: We present results from a reanalysis of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey, conducted at 350 MHz with the Green Bank Telescope between 2009 and 2020, covering the sky with declinations $δ>-40^\circ$. We searched the survey data using an FFT-based periodicity search, with candidate selection extending to very low spectral signal-to-noise ratios and summing up to 32 harmonics. From the 60 promising candidates identified in this search, we confirmed 51 new pulsars using the Green bank and CHIME. We also used a direct folding search method (DFSM) to search for slow pulsars between 500 ms and 10 s. Of the 51 pulsars identified in the FFT search, 43 fall within this period range, all of which were found by the DFSM. The DFSM also found an additional pulsar that had been missed during the inspection of the FFT candidates. Most of the new discoveries are canonical pulsars, with spin periods ranging from 299 ms to 4.4 s and dispersion measures from 10 to 192 $\rm pc \, cm^{-3}$. We also found a binary millisecond pulsar with a spin period of 3.2 ms in a 4.5-d orbit. We redetected 855 pulsars in the data, 825 of which were found in the FFT search. Within the effective parameter space of our periodicity search, the FFT search recovered $\sim$98 % of the known pulsars within the survey sensitivity limits. After accounting for previously reported pulsars whose observations were not processed or whose parameters lay outside our search range, the updated GBNCC census now includes 964 pulsars.

AI.method: 使用绿岸望远镜（Green Bank Telescope）2009 年至 2020 年在 350 MHz 开展的 GBNCC 巡天数据，覆盖赤纬 $δ>-40^\circ$。采用基于 FFT 的周期性搜索，候选体选择扩展至非常低的光谱信噪比并累加至 32 个谐波；另用直接折叠搜索方法（DFSM）搜索 500 ms 至 10 s 的慢脉冲星。新脉冲星用 Green bank 和 CHIME 确认。

AI.conclusion: 在计入此前已报告但其观测未被处理或其参数位于搜索范围之外的脉冲星后，更新后的 GBNCC 普查现在包含 964 颗脉冲星。该结果表明重新分析与扩展搜索可提高巡天脉冲星回收率并扩充脉冲星普查。根据摘要无法判断该工作与磁星、快速射电暴（FRB）或单脉冲发射等主题的具体联系。

title: A0538-66: A transient ultraluminous X-ray source with a relativistic outflow, 69ms pulsations, and anomalous optical activity
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: A0538-66 is a peculiar Be/X-ray binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud, hosting the fastest spinning neutron star of its class (~69ms) and showing the brightest optical bursts of any system of this type. We report four XMM-Newton observations obtained near periastron in 2025, together with MAXI and REM monitoring, and a reanalysis of archival RXTE data. On 30 September 2025 the source reached L_X~1.5E39 erg/s (0.2-10 keV), the highest level since 1980, and in February, May, and August 2026, MAXI detected similarly bright outbursts. During the XMM-Newton observation taken on 30 September 2025, we detected the pulsations, measuring P_spin=69.25878(2) ms and dP_spin/dt=6.58(9)E-10 s/s; the pulsed fraction was low (~3% in 1-10 keV), increased with energy, and the soft and hard pulse profiles were shifted by half a cycle. A new detection in RXTE data of 3 December 1998 gives a faster spin period of P_spin=68.88813(28) ms. The XMM-Newton/RGS spectra show emission lines from photoionised plasma at rest and blueshifted absorption lines that imply an outflow at ~0.12c. This indicates a highly super-Eddington accretion rate and an intrinsic L_X~1.5E39 erg/s, and it makes A0538-66 a transient ultra-luminous X-ray pulsar, a class of which only a few objects are known so far. Since 2023 the optical bursts observed by REM have become longer and brighter, resembling those of the 1980s, but most of them lack a luminous X-ray counterpart (L_X>1E37 erg/s). We interpret these results in terms of a radiation pressure dominated accretion disc whose geometrically thick inner regions intermittently screen the innermost emitting regions.

title: Low-frequency spectra and scattering of pulsars towards the Gum Nebula with the MWA
comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: Context. The Gum Nebula is a nearby ionised complex with sight-line-dependent pulsar propagation. Aims. We test whether a smooth ionised structure can explain low-frequency spectral turnovers and pulse broadening, or whether smaller-scale material is required. Methods. We analysed Murchison Widefield Array observations of six pulsars at 80--240 MHz, combining sub-band flux densities with literature data. We compared power-law, free--free absorption (FFA), and turnover-constrained broken-power-law (BPL) spectra, and modelled scattering through pulse-profile convolution. PSR J0820-4114 and the Vela pulsar were fitted jointly across frequency. Results. All six spectra depart from a single power law. FFA is favoured for PSRs J0737-3039A and J0820-4114, and BPL for J0742-2822 and J0835-4510; the other two classifications depend on assumed error floors. Conditional FFA solutions imply emission measures of $10^4$--$10^5$ pc cm$^{-6}$ for electron temperatures of $3\times10^3$--$10^4$ K, far exceeding smooth-shell expectations. PSRs J0737-3039A and J0837-4135 have scattering laws consistent with $τ_{\rm sc}\proptoν^{-4}$. We obtain $α_{\rm sc}=-3.07\pm0.11$ for J0742-2822 and $-1.59\pm0.44$ for J0820-4114 using a joint two-component model. The Vela pulsar is best described by an effective thick-screen model with $α_{\rm sc}\simeq-2.74$. Neither tested Galactic electron-density model reproduces both independent distances and low-frequency scattering uniformly. Conclusions. The results favour a structured Gum--Vela magneto-ionic environment in which neighbouring sight lines probe different absorbing and scattering material; these effects need not arise in the same plasma component.

title: Fast Radio Bursts from Monster Shocks and Flares of Inspiraling Binary Neutron Stars: A Kinetic Model for Double Pulsar
summary: The coalescence of binary neutron star systems offers unprecedented possibilities for multimessenger observations, including the detection of gravitational waves, gamma-ray bursts, kilonovae, and potentially fast radio bursts. For a detailed investigation of the latter, one requires a kinetic plasma model to describe the interacting magnetospheres of the stars. We present a three-dimensional particle-in-cell kinetic simulation of the combined magnetosphere of a binary neutron star in which the two stars physically orbit one another so that the orbital motion itself twists the magnetic loops. We find that the stellar magnetic-field intensity ratio controls the emergence of flares, while the stellar spins set the direction and modulation of the flare. We identify four spatially and dynamically distinct regions of strong electromagnetic energy release: (i) an expanding fast magnetosonic wave that steepens into a monster shock, (ii) a plasma flare being pushed by (iii) an expanding fireball and containing (iv) a reconnecting current sheet. The fast magnetosonic wave is a promising source of coherent radio emission. It is released when orbital motion cuts a closed plasma loop. The electric and magnetic wave amplitudes are similar and reach that of the background magnetic field. Our kinetic treatment yields particle spectra and plasma structures that can be used to assess coherent emission in kinetic-scale simulations. In conclusion, the stellar orbital motion constitutes a driving channel distinct from models with spin-driven magnetospheric twisting.

AI.abstract_translation: 双中子星系统的并合为多信使观测提供了前所未有的可能性，包括引力波、伽马射线暴、千新星以及潜在的快速射电暴（FRB）的探测。为了对后者进行详细研究，需要一个动理学等离子体模型来描述两星相互作用的磁层。我们提出了一个双中子星联合磁层的三维粒子模拟（particle-in-cell）动理学模拟，其中两颗星实际地相互绕转，使得轨道运动本身扭转磁环。我们发现，恒星磁场强度比对耀斑的出现起控制作用，而恒星自转则决定耀斑的方向和调制。我们识别出四个在空间上和动力学上不同的强电磁能量释放区域：(i) 一个膨胀的快速磁声波，它陡化为怪物激波，(ii) 一个等离子体耀斑，它被 (iii) 一个膨胀的火球推动，并包含 (iv) 一个重联电流片。快速磁声波是相干射电辐射的一个有希望的来源。它是在轨道运动切断一个闭合等离子体环时释放的。电场和磁波的振幅相近，并达到背景磁场的量级。我们的动理学处理给出了粒子谱和等离子体结构，可用于评估动理学尺度模拟中的相干辐射。总之，恒星轨道运动构成了一条不同于自转驱动磁层扭转模型的驱动通道。

title: Two sides of the same spin: tracking optical and radio pulsations of SAX J1808.4-3658 from outburst to quiescence
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: High-time-resolution optical and UV observations have revealed bright coherent pulsations from accreting millisecond pulsars, exceeding the luminosity expected from thermal emission from NS hotspots or X-ray reflection by the accretion disk. Characterizing optical pulsations over a wide range of accretion rates through coordinated multi-wavelength observations can shed light on their origin. We present a timing study of the AMSP SAX J1808.4-3658 during its 2022 outburst and quiescence, using optical TNG/SiFAP2 observations, simultaneous NICER X-ray data, LCO optical monitoring, and MeerKAT radio observations in quiescence. During the outburst, we detect coherent optical pulsations with pulsed luminosities of 1.3x10^(30)erg/s. Combined with previous detections, our results suggest that the optical pulsed amplitude increases as the X-ray flux decreases. The X-ray and optical pulsed luminosities show opposite trends with X-ray luminosity, suggesting different responses to changes in the accretion rate. We measure X-ray-to-optical delays of 0.88+-0.04ms and 0.51+-0.03 ms in two outburst observations, indicating that the relative timing between the signals is not constant. Together with the spectral energy distribution, these results support different emission mechanisms: non-thermal emission from relativistic particles for optical pulsations and channeled accretion onto the NS surface for X-ray pulsations. During quiescence, we detect no coherent optical pulsations, obtaining a 95% confidence upper limit of <2.2x10^(29)erg/s on the optical pulsed luminosity, corresponding to an optical efficiency comparable to those of spider radio millisecond pulsars. Simultaneous MeerKAT observations reveal no radio pulsations down to ~10μJy, significantly improving previous constraints but not excluding an active rotation-powered pulsar whose radio emission may be absorbed by intra-binary material.

title: Evidence for Distinct One-Off and Repeating Subpopulations in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: The Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) has published its second catalog of 3,641 fast radio bursts (FRBs). While this sample includes 981 bursts from 83 repeating sources, only 2.3% of CHIME FRBs are observed to repeat. This raises the question of whether the FRB population truly consists of a single repeating population or includes a distinct subpopulation of one-off sources. We apply Simulation Based Inference (SBI), a likelihood-free machine learning framework, to model the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 dataset, testing eight FRB population models, half of which include a subpopulation of truly one-off sources. The current catalog strongly and decisively favors models including such a subpopulation, with the best-fitting model combining a log-normal burst rate distribution, a Poissonian wait-time distribution, and a one-off subpopulation. This preference is corroborated by an independent random forest classifier and by the ability of one-off models to naturally reproduce the hyperactive repeating sources present in the catalog without having been trained on them. We place upper limits on the potentially observable CHIME/FRB population of 36,000 repeating sources and 19 one-off sources per day in the CHIME sky. Models with a one-off subpopulation naturally account for the hyperactive repeating sources present in the catalog without having been trained on them, providing an independent consistency check on our results. We predict the repeater percentage will fall below 2% in the next five years, eventually declining to ~0.5% as the sample saturates with one-off detections.

title: In-flight Timing Calibration of the Follow-up X-Ray Telescope on Board the Einstein Probe
summary: After the launch of Einstein Probe (EP), pulsars are observed to calibrate the timing system of the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) by measuring the times of arrival (TOAs). FXT has two independently operating modules, namely FXTA and FXTB, each equipped with the Wolter-I optics and the pnCCD camera. For scientific observations, each pnCCD has three distinct readout modes that differ in frame cycles, the full frame mode (FF, 50 ms per frame), the partial windowed mode (PW, 2.2 ms per frame), and the timing mode (TM, 23.68 $μ$s per row, 9.4352 ms per frame). Thus, 1RXS J170849.0--400910 with the spin period of 11 s is observed in FF, PSR B1509--58 (150 ms) in PW, and Crab pulsar (33 ms) in TM as well as PSR B1821--24 (3.05 ms) and PSR B1937+21 (1.56 ms). The TOAs of these pulsars measured by FXTA and FXTB are compared with the results of NICER, and for Crab pulsar with the Jodrell Bank Monthly Ephemeris (JBE). Results verify that the timing system of FXTA and FXTB in FF, PW, and TM modes are consistent with each other, and are in good alignment with NICER. The measured advance of the Crab pulsar's main peak relative to JBE is $357^{\pm14(stat)}_{\pm54(sys)} μ$s in FXTA and $394^{\pm14(stat)}_{\pm67(sys)} μ$s in FXTB. Based on measurements of PSR B1821--24 and PSR B1937+21, the preliminary absolute timing accuracy is estimated to be 6 $μ$s for FXTA and 31 $μ$s for FXTB in TM mode. Additionally, the systematic delay of FXTA timing results relative to FXTB is found to be $20^{\pm19(stat)}_{\pm21(sys)} μ$s.

title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
summary: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.
